title: SLA linguistics and error-budget runbook for Dedicated capacity
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: Customers buying Dedicated capacity expect contractual guarantees that align technical telemetry with commercial remedies. This ticket defines canonical SLA language, an operational runbook for computing and tracking error budgets, and the precise crediting math used for remediation. Scope: 1) Define SLOs (availability, quantile throughput, degraded-serve windows) and exact measurement windows; 2) Provide canonical contract clause templates for legal/CS; 3) Specify an error-budget computation algorithm (per billing period) and crediting matrix; 4) Define autoscaler interlock behavior (how and when autoscale events modify SLA measurement and mitigation); 5) Operational telemetry queries and dashboards for customer-facing reports; 6) Acceptance criteria and rollout plan for public-facing contract language. Proposed metrics and definitions: - Serve Availability (SA): percentage of requests accepted and successfully served within the committed latency quantile (default: 99th percentile latency <= committed threshold) over a rolling 30-day window. - Throughput Commitment (TC): committed tokens-per-minute or requests-per-second floor measured as the 5th percentile of 1-minute-sampled throughput over a calendar month. - Degradation Window: any continuous 5-minute interval where SA < target or TC < committed floor. Error budget computation (monthly): - Start with 100% of monthly entitlement. - For availability: error_budget_avail = (1 - SA_target) * total_minutes_in_month. - Burn occurs when measured SA in a minute is below target; burn_minutes = max(0, SA_target - SA_measured) * 1 minute. - For throughput: compute shortfall_tokens = max(0, TC_committed - TC_measured) aggregated over minute samples. - Normalize throughput shortfall into equivalent minutes using baseline throughput conversion table (configurable per contract). Crediting matrix (example): - Minor deviation (1-24 minutes equivalent burn in month): 5% service credit on that months invoice line for Dedicated capacity. - Moderate (25-240 minutes): 20% credit plus committed capacity review with customer success. - Severe (>240 minutes or repeated incidents exceeding thresholds): escalation to executive review and pro-rata refund on the Dedicated capacity fee for the affected days plus free burst credits for next billing cycle. Autoscale interlock rules: - When autoscaler is actively scaling up due to detected saturation and the customer has enabled burst credits, we classify the window as "autoscale-assisted" and exclude the automatic scale-up period (from scale trigger to full readiness) from Customer-facing SLA burn only if the autoscaler adhered to configured cooldowns and no operator error occurred. - If autoscaler fails to provision capacity due to capacity-exhaustion in underlying region, that counts as platform degradation and counts against the error budget. Measurement and data sources: - Canonical source of truth is telemetry in Observability (Prometheus/OLAP) with daily reconciliation job producing a signed measurement report per account. - All SLA measurements are anchored to event timestamps in UTC and aligned to customer billing timezone for final invoice credits. Contract language (sample clause): "Dedicated Serve Commitment: Redwood Inference will provide Dedicated capacity with a Serve Availability target of 99.95% measured over a 30-day period (the \"SLA\"). If Redwood fails to meet the SLA for a given billing period, Customer may be eligible for service credits as described in the Service Credit Table. Service credits are Redwoods sole and exclusive remedy for any failure to meet the SLA. To obtain a credit, Customer must submit a claim within 30 days after the end of the billing period with sufficient evidence (logs and the signed measurement report)." Edge cases and trade-offs: - Should regional failovers count as a single incident or multiple? Proposal: count per-customer-affected region and apply proportional credits. - How to handle noisy probes from customer traffic patterns? Proposal: require a minimum request volume before throughput guarantees apply (e.g., 1k tokens/min sustained for 1 hour) to avoid credits for low-volume statistical anomalies. Deliverables: - Canonical SLA clause text (legal-reviewed) - Error-budget computation notebook (python) and unit tests - Measurement ELT job to produce signed measurement reports - Customer-facing FAQ and claim submission flow - Ops runbook for investigating and reconciling SLA claims (including required artifacts) Rollout plan: 1) Draft language and math (this ticket) 2) Legal review and CS feedback (2 weeks) 3) Implement measurement job and dashboards (ENG sprint) 4) Pilot with 3 existing Dedicated customers and iterate 5) Bake into sales contracts and public help center page
acceptance_criteria: Legal-approved SLA clause text checked into contract template library

Signed measurement report generator runs nightly and is available in customer portal for pilot accounts

Product + CS pilot completed with two-way feedback documented and any contract updates applied
